div.l: GRete chere made our ost to vs euerychon
And to supper sette he vs anon
He serued vs wyth vytaylle at the beste
Stronge was the wyne ⁊and well drynke vs lyste
A semely man our ost was wyth alle
For to be a marchall in a lordis halle
A large man he was wyth eyen stepe
A fayrer burgeys is there none in chepe
Bolde of his speche and well was he taught
And of manhode lackyd he ryght nought
Eke therto was he ryght a mery man
And after supper to playn he began
And spake of myrthe amonge other thynges
Whan that we had made our rekenynges
He sayd thus now lordynges truely
Ye be to me ryght welcome hertly
For by my trouth yf I shall not lye
I sawe not this yere so mery a company
At onys in this herborow as now
Feyne wolde I do you myrthe yf I wyst how
And of a myrthe I am ryght now bethought
To do you ease and it shall coste you nought
Ye go to Caunterbury ward god you spede
The blysfull martyr quyte you your mede
And well ye wote as ye go by the waye
Ye shapen you to talke and to playe
For truely comfort ne myrthe is noue
To ryde by the waye dombe as a stone
And therfore wyll I make you dysport
As I sayd erst and do you comfort
And yf it lyketh you all by one assent
For to stonde at my Iugement
And for to werke as I shall you say
To morow whan ye ryde on the way
Now by my faders soule that is ded
But ye be mery I shall yeue you my hed
Holde vp your honde wythout more speche
Our counsell shall not longe be to seche
Vs thought it was not worth to make vs wys
And graunted hym without more aduys
And bad hym saye his verdyt as hym leste
Lordynges quod he now herkeneth for the best
But take it not I pray you in disdeyne
This is the poynt to speke it short and playne
